questions.question:
**Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order.** 

There needs to be a 

P: more coordinated effort 

Q: forest diseases in India 

R: towards dealing with
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'PRQ'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **"Q" **can't be first in sequence since *forest diseases *can't be preceded by '**a**.'
 
• **"****R"** doesn't fit in either (*a towards = doesn't make grammatical or contextual sense)*.
 
• Thus, **"P"** is first. Rule out 3) and 4). You can't end a sentence with a preposition. So, R can't be last (ends with **with**).
 
• Hence, Option 1 i.e. **'PRQ'*** *is the correct answer.

***So the correct sentence is***→*There needs to be a more coordinated effort towards dealing with forest diseases in India.*

questions.question:
**A sentence has been given in Active/Passive Voice. Out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in**** ****Passive/Active Voice.** 

A policeman caught her.

options.text: She was caught by a policeman.
She is catch by a policeman.
She is caught by a policeman.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'She was caught by a policeman'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Let's see the steps to change the Active voice into the passive voice.
 
 
• **Firstly,** check the tense of the sentence because the tense in the A/P voice doesn't change.
 
• **Secondly,** look for the object in the sentence. The object of the sentence gives the reply of what/whom.
 
• **Thirdly, **if the object of the sentence is not given then look for the infinitive and change the infinitive verb into the passive voice.
 
• **Fourth,** the subject of the sentence in the active voice changes into the object of the sentence in the passive voice, and the object becomes the subject of the sentence.
 
• *The given sentence is in the past simple tense. So the structure of the verb is 'was + V₃'*
 
 
 
• **So the correct sentence is-** *She was caught by a policeman.*

questions.question:
**A sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect Speech. Out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in**** ****Indirect/ Direct Speech.** 

Raju wrote, “I will be going to Mumbai tomorrow."

options.text: Raju wrote that he will be going to Mumbai tomorrow.
Raju wrote that he would be going to Mumbai the day before.
Raju wrote that he would be going to Mumbai the day after.
Raju wrote that he should be gone to Mumbai the next day.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Raju wrote that he would be going to Mumbai the day after'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Let's see the steps we make while doing the conversion of Direct speech into Indirect speech-**

 
 
• *If the reporting verb is in the past tense, then the direct sentence is changed in its past tense.*
 
• *The tense of direct speech remains unchanged when the reporting verb is in the present or future tense.*
 
• *If the direct sentence contains the universal truth, then it remains unchanged in the Indirect Speech.*
 
• *The reporting verb said/said to is changed in asked, demanded, ordered, enquired as per the nature of the sentence.*
 
• *While a sentence starts with the reporting verb then at the conversion time if /whether is used as the joining clause.*
 
• *In case the sentence starts from the “Wh” question word, then no extra conjunction is used.*
 
• *The first person in reported speech changes according to the subject of reporting speech.*
 
• *In Reported Speech change of the second person depends on the object of reporting speech.*
 
• *The third person remains unchanged.*
 
 
 
• So according to these steps, **the correct answer is** *'Raju wrote that he would be going to Mumbai the day after'*
